newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian firms agree to cut greenhouse gases.
newsitem.headline: Australian firms agree to cut greenhouse gases.

text.p: Australia, under international fire over greenhouse gas emissions, said on Wednesday 11 more major firms had joined its programme to cut carbon dioxide emissions by 15 percent by 2000.
Resources Minister Warwick Parer said a total of 31 companies, accounting for 45 percent of all Australia's greenhouse emissions, had now signed on to the government's Greenhouse Challenge programme.

The challenge is a government-industry programme in which companies outline plans to cut emissions of carbon dioxide -- the main gas blamed for global warming -- and how they will use energy more efficiently.
"This is an impressive result overall," he said in a statement.
"Not only are we seeing leading edge research and development by some of these companies, we are also witnessing innovative management approaches," he said.
Companies who have joined the challenge have committed to cutting carbon dioxide emissions by a total 16 million tonnes a year by 2000, representing a 15-percent cut on current levels.

Canberra is battling international pressure, particularly from the United States and European governments, to agree to compulsory targets for cuts in greenhouse emissions by developed countries after 2000.
Australia is among a group of nations expected to oppose compulsory targets at an international conference in Kyoto, Japan, in December this year.
